hook.text: In 1952, a student named David Huffman solved a homework problem his professor couldn't. He invented optimal coding.

buildup.text: Huffman coding builds a binary tree bottom-up: merge the two least probable symbols, repeat.

discovery.text: The result is a prefix code where common symbols get short codewords and rare ones get long ones.

twist.text: Huffman codes are provably optimal among symbol-by-symbol prefix codes. No other method beats them.

climax.text: JPEG, MP3, and ZIP all use Huffman coding as one of their compression stages.

punchline.text: A homework assignment that changed computing forever.

quiz.question: How does Huffman coding build its code tree?
options: Bottom-up by merging least probable symbols
